verdict: Intuit's tax-season quarter delivered: revenue rose 10% to $8.6B and net income 9% to $3.1B, powered by TurboTax's assisted-tax growth and a 19% jump in QuickBooks' online ecosystem.

kpis.label: TurboTax revenue
kpis.note: +7% YoY, on higher prices and assisted tax

segments.name: Global Business Solutions
segments.note: QuickBooks and Mailchimp for small and mid-sized businesses. The online ecosystem brought in $2.5B (+19%), with QuickBooks Online accounting revenue up 22% — price rises, customer growth and richer mix.

segments.name: Consumer
segments.note: TurboTax ($4,364M in its peak quarter), Credit Karma ($631M, +15%) and ProTax for professional preparers ($278M, flat). This is the segment that makes Q3 Intuit's biggest quarter of the year.

flow.costPlain: Running Intuit's cloud services and customer support ($1,317M), product costs ($14M), and amortization of acquired technology ($43M).

opex.name: Selling and marketing
opex.note: Selling TurboTax, QuickBooks and Credit Karma — tax season is when the year's customers are won.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building QuickBooks, TurboTax, Credit Karma and Mailchimp — increasingly, AI agents that do bookkeeping and tax prep.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day.

opex.name: Amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of customer relationships and other assets from acquisitions like Mailchimp and Credit Karma.

otherDetail: Interest and other income, net of $97M, less $70M of interest expense, added $27M.

follow100Note: This is Intuit at full stretch: in tax season it keeps $35.81 of every $100 — compare the off-season quarter, when it keeps far less. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Tax season is still the main event
takeaways.text: Consumer revenue was $5,273M, 62% of the company. TurboTax grew 7% to $4,364M — fewer federal returns, but higher prices and fast growth in assisted tax (TurboTax Live is guided to +36% for the full year) more than made up for it.

takeaways.title: QuickBooks' online engine keeps compounding
takeaways.text: Global Business Solutions grew 15% to $3,285M, with the online ecosystem up 19% to $2.5B and QuickBooks Online accounting revenue up 22%. Mid-market businesses are growing north of 30%.

takeaways.title: Cash comes back to shareholders
takeaways.text: Intuit bought back $1.6B of stock in the quarter and ended it with $6.8B of cash and investments against $6.2B of debt. It also raised its full-year FY26 revenue guidance alongside this print.

oneTimers: Share-based compensation was $485M in the quarter — counted in GAAP profit, and the main reason non-GAAP EPS ($12.80) sits well above the GAAP figure ($11.09).
There was no restructuring charge this quarter (versus $1M a year ago) — unusually for Intuit's recent prints, the GAAP numbers are clean of big one-off charges.
Segment split: Consumer revenue is stated in the release; Global Business Solutions is the remainder of total revenue.
